article.story: AUSTIN, Texas -- — Jayda Clark scored 19 points, Isi Etute added 18 and No. 6 Texas remained undefeated by rolling to a 96-45 victory against Southeastern Louisiana on Wednesday night. All-American Madison Booker had 14 points, 10 assists and six steals for Texas (7-0). Texas coach Vic Schaefer had to do some rebuilding when Jordan Lee, Aaliyah Crump and Justice Carlton transferred to other schools after the Longhorns reached the Final Four last season. One new starting guard, the sophomore Clark, came from Australia during the off season. She converted 7 of 11 from the field, including a pair of 3-pointers, and made three steals Wednesday. Another starting guard, Zya Vann, transferred from Oklahoma. Vann missed the game Wednesday for an unspecified reason, according to a team spokesman. Freshman Addison Bjorn, making her first start in place of Vann, scored 10 points in 18 minutes. Starting center Bryan Cunningham had 11 points and seven rebounds. Etute, her freshman backup, hit 7 of 11 shots while also filling in at power forward. Texas had a 58-28 advantage scoring in the paint and 32-2 on fast-break points. Southeastern Louisiana (2-5) has experienced a rough time against power conference opponents this season, losing to No. 9 LSU 129-35, No. 15 TCU 106-47 and Texas Tech 88-51. On Wednesday, the played most of the game without Natalie Huff, their second-leading scorer who left early in the second quarter with an injury. Aliyah Collins led Southeastern Louisiana with 16 points. The Lions hit just 34.6% and committed 26 turnovers, both enabling Texas to establish its edge in fast-break points. Up next Southeastern Louisiana: Hosts Houston Christian on Dec. 3. Texas: Visits Southeast Missouri State on Sunday.
